title.zh: 卷一百二十二 周書13: 宗室列傳二
title.en: Volume 122 Book of Later Zhou 24: Biographies 2 - Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷一百二十二 周書13: 宗室列傳二 Volume 122 Book of Later Zhou 24: Biographies 2 - Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 剡王侗，太祖子，初名青哥，漢末遇害。

translations.literal: Prince of Shan Tong, a son of Taizu, was originally named Qingge; he was killed at the end of the Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong of Shan was a son of Taizu; his childhood name was Qingge, and he was murdered in the final days of the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，詔贈太尉，賜名侗。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict posthumously conferred on him the rank of Grand Commandant and granted him the name Tong.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu came to the throne, he ordered Tong posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and given the formal name Tong.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年追封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He received a posthumous enfeoffment in the fourth year of the Xiande era.

sentences.zh: 杞王信，太祖子，初名意哥，漢末遇害。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xin, a son of Taizu, was originally named Yige; he was killed at the end of the Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin of Qi was another son of Taizu; born Yige, he too was slain in the closing days of the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，詔贈司空，賜名信。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict posthumously conferred on him the rank of Minister of Works and granted him the name Xin.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Taizu posthumously named him Xin and honored him as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年追封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He too was enfeoffed posthumously in Xiande 4.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （案：太祖諸子蚤歲遇害，本無事跡。

translations.literal: Annotation: the several sons of Taizu were killed in their early years and originally had no deeds to record.
translations.idiomatic: Editor's note: Taizu's sons were murdered young and left virtually no deeds worth recording.

sentences.zh: 原本過於簡略，疑有刪節，今據《歐陽史·家人傳》云：初，帝舉兵於魏，漢以兵圍帝第，時張貴妃與諸子青哥、意哥，侄守筠、奉超、定哥皆被誅。

translations.literal: The original text is excessively brief and is suspected of having been abridged; now according to the "Biographies of the Imperial Family" in Ouyang's History it says: at first, when the Emperor raised troops in Wei, the Han sent troops to besiege the Emperor's residence; at that time the Honored Consort Zhang and the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge, were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The base text is so terse that passages may have been cut; the following is drawn from Ouyang Xiu's family biographies. When the future Taizu first took up arms in Wei, the Later Han besieged his household. The honored consort Zhang, the boys Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 青哥、意哥不知其母誰氏。

translations.literal: It is not known whose sons Qingge and Yige were by their mothers.
translations.idiomatic: The mothers of Qingge and Yige are unknown.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，詔故第二子青哥贈太尉，賜名侗；

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict posthumously conferred on the former second son Qingge the rank of Grand Commandant and granted him the name Tong;
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu acceded, he posthumously named his former second son Qingge Tong and honored him as Grand Commandant;

sentences.zh: 第三子意哥贈司空，賜名信。

translations.literal: the third son Yige was posthumously conferred Minister of Works and granted the name Xin.
translations.idiomatic: his third son Yige he named Xin and raised to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 皇侄守筠贈左領軍衛將軍，以「筠」聲近「榮」，為世宗避，更名守願；

translations.literal: The imperial nephew Shoujun was posthumously made General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty; because the sound of "jun" was close to "rong," to avoid the taboo for Shizong he was renamed Shouyuan;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial nephew Shoujun was made General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty, but because jun sounded like rong—the character in Shizong's personal name—he was renamed Shouyuan;

sentences.zh: 奉超贈左監門衛將軍；

translations.literal: Fengchao was posthumously made General of the Left Gate Guards;
translations.idiomatic: Fengchao was honored as General of the Left Gate Guards;

sentences.zh: 定哥贈左千牛衛將軍，賜名遜。

translations.literal: Dingge was posthumously made General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guards and granted the name Xun.
translations.idiomatic: and Dingge was made General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guards and given the name Xun.

sentences.zh: 世宗顯德四年夏四月癸未，詔曰：「禮以緣情，恩以悼往，矧在友於之列，尤鐘惻愴之情。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, in the fourth month, on the day guiwei, Shizong issued an edict saying: "Rites follow feeling; grace mourns what is past; how much more among the ranks of brotherly affection is there especially deep compassionate feeling.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day in the fourth month of Xiande 4, Shizong proclaimed: "Ritual springs from human feeling, and favor should mourn the dead—above all among brothers, where compassion runs deepest.

sentences.zh: 故皇弟贈太保侗、贈司空信，景運初啟，天年不登，俾予終鮮，實動予懷。

translations.literal: The late imperial younger brothers, the posthumously titled Grand Guardian Tong and Minister of Works Xin, when the auspicious fortune had just begun, did not complete their allotted years, leaving me without brothers to the end—this truly moves my heart.
translations.idiomatic: My late brothers, Grand Guardian Tong and Minister of Works Xin, died just as fortune was turning and never lived out their years, leaving me alone among my kin—a grief that pierces me still.

sentences.zh: 侗可贈太傅，追封剡王；

translations.literal: Tong may be posthumously made Grand Tutor and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Shan;
translations.idiomatic: Let Tong be raised to Grand Tutor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shan;

sentences.zh: 信司徒，杞王。

translations.literal: Xin as Minister over the Masses, Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: and Xin as Minister over the Masses and Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「故皇從弟贈左領軍衛將軍守願、贈左監門衛將軍奉超、贈左千牛衛將軍遜等，頃因季世，不享遐齡，每念非辜，難忘有慟。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "The late imperial cousins, the posthumously titled General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty Shouyuan, General of the Left Gate Guards Fengchao, and General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guards Xun and others, recently because of the troubled age did not enjoy long life; whenever I think of their innocence, I cannot forget my grief.
translations.idiomatic: " A second edict read: "My late cousins Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun—honored respectively as generals of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty, the Left Gate Guards, and the Left Thousand-Ox Guards—perished young in violent times. Remembering their undeserved deaths, I cannot lay grief aside.

sentences.zh: 守願可贈左衛大將軍，奉超右衛大將軍，遜右武衛大將軍。」）〉

translations.literal: Shouyuan may be posthumously made Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard." (End of editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: Shouyuan shall be Grand General of the Left Guard, Fengchao of the Right Guard, and Xun of the Right Martial Guard." (End of editorial note.)

sentences.zh: 越王宗誼，世宗子，漢末遇害。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Zongyi, a son of Shizong, was killed at the end of the Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zongyi of Yue was a son of Shizong who was murdered in the final days of the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年追封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He received posthumous enfeoffment in Xiande 4.

sentences.zh: 曹王宗讓，世宗子，顯德六年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Cao Zongrang, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zongrang of Cao, another son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in Xiande 6.

sentences.zh: 紀王熙謹，世宗子，顯德六年封，皇朝乾德二年卒。

translations.literal: Prince of Ji Xi Jinjian, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande and died in the second year of Qiande of the present dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi Jinjian of Ji, also Shizong's son, was enfeoffed in Xiande 6 and died in the second year of the Song Qiande era.

sentences.zh: 蘄王熙誨，世宗子，顯德六年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xi Hui, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi Hui of Qi was enfeoffed in Xiande 6, likewise a son of Shizong.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史·家人傳》云：世宗子七人，長曰宜哥，次二皆未名，次曰恭皇帝，次曰熙讓，次曰熙謹，次曰熙誨，皆不知其母為誰氏，宜哥與其二皆為漢誅。

translations.literal: The "Biographies of the Imperial Family" in Ouyang's History says: Shizong had seven sons; the eldest was called Yige, the next two were both unnamed, the next was the Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jinjian, and Xi Hui; it is not known who their mothers were; Yige and the other two were all executed by the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu's family biographies record seven sons of Shizong: the eldest Yige, two younger boys still unnamed, then the future Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jinjian, and Xi Hui. Their mothers are unknown. Yige and the two unnamed boys were killed by the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，詔賜皇孫名，誼贈左驍衛大將軍，誠左武衛大將軍，諴左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict granted names to the imperial grandsons: Yi was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Cheng Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and Yan Grand General of the Left Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu acceded he named his grandsons: Yi became Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Cheng of the Left Martial Guard, and Yan of the Left Garrison.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，君臣請封宗室，世宗以謂為國日淺，恩信未及於人，須功德大成，慶流於世，而後議之可也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande, ministers and subjects requested enfeoffment of the imperial clan; Shizong considered that the state was still young in days, that favor and trust had not yet reached the people, and that one must wait until merit and virtue were fully achieved and blessings flowed through the age before such matters could be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande 3 the court asked to enfeoff the imperial clan. Shizong replied that the dynasty was still young, its grace had not yet won men's hearts, and titles should wait until great deeds had been done and blessings could be shared with the realm.

sentences.zh: 明年夏四月癸未，先封太祖諸子。

translations.literal: In the summer of the next year, on the day guiwei of the fourth month, he first enfeoffed the several sons of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The following fourth month, on guiwei day, he enfeoffed Taizu's slain sons first.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「父子之道，聖賢不忘，再思夭閼之端，愈動悲傷之抱。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The way of father and son—the sages do not forget it; thinking again of the beginning of untimely obstruction, one's embrace of grief and sorrow is stirred all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He also proclaimed: "The bond between father and son is what the sages never forget. To dwell again on a son's early death is to reopen the wound.

sentences.zh: 故皇子左驍衛大將軍誼、左武衛大將軍誠、左屯衛大將軍諴等，載惟往事，有足傷懷，宜增一字之封，仍贈三臺之秩。

translations.literal: The late princes, Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Yi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Cheng, and Grand General of the Left Garrison Yan and others—reflecting on past events, there is ample cause for wounded feeling; they should receive an added character in their enfeoffment and still be granted ranks among the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: My sons Yi, Cheng, and Yan—honored as generals of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Martial Guard, and Garrison—deserve remembrance that still pains me. Let each receive a fuller princely title and a post in the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 誼可贈太尉，追封越王；

translations.literal: Yi may be posthumously made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Yi shall be Grand Commandant and Prince of Yue;

sentences.zh: 誠太傅，吳王；

translations.literal: Cheng as Grand Tutor, Prince of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Grand Tutor and Prince of Wu;

sentences.zh: 諴太保，韓王。

translations.literal: Yan as Grand Guardian, Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: and Yan Grand Guardian and Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 」而皇子在者皆不封。

translations.literal: " Yet the princes who were still alive were all left without enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: " Living princes, however, received no titles.

sentences.zh: 六年，北復三關，遇疾還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, recovering the three passes in the north, he fell ill and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixth year Shizong reconquered the three northern passes, fell ill, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，皇子宗訓特進左衛上將軍，封梁王，而宗讓亦拜左驍衛上將軍，封燕國公。

translations.literal: On guiwei day of the sixth month, the prince Zongxun was specially advanced to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, while Zongrang was also appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day in the sixth month Prince Zongxun was made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Prince of Liang, while Zongrang became General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry and Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 後十日而世宗崩，梁王即位，是為恭皇帝。

translations.literal: Ten days later Shizong died; the Prince of Liang took the throne—this was Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Shizong died. The Prince of Liang succeeded him as Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，宗讓更名熙讓，封曹王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year, Zongrang was renamed Xi Rang and enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: That August Zongrang took the name Xi Rang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 熙謹、熙誨皆前未封爵，遂拜熙謹右武衛大將軍，封紀王；

translations.literal: Xi Jinjian and Xi Hui had both previously received no noble rank; thereupon Xi Jinjian was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jinjian and Xi Hui had never held titles; now Xi Jinjian was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and Prince of Ji;

sentences.zh: 熙誨左領軍衛大將軍，封蘄王。

translations.literal: Xi Hui was made Grand General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: and Xi Hui Grand General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty and Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年十月，熙謹卒，熙讓、熙誨不知其所終。）

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Qiande, Xi Jinjian died; the final fates of Xi Rang and Xi Hui are unknown. (End of editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jinjian died in the tenth month of Qiande 2; what became of Xi Rang and Xi Hui is not recorded. (End of editorial note.)
